html:
The Pawtucket were an Algonquian people of the lower Merrimack River valley in northeastern Massachusetts and southern New Hampshire. They were closely tied to the Pennacook upriver, and in the 1600s both followed the great sachem Passaconaway. Pawtucket Falls, at today's Lowell, was a major fishing place.

An epidemic from 1616 to 1619, brought by European ships, killed most of the coastal peoples of New England just before the English colonists arrived. The survivors faced the growing Massachusetts Bay Colony. Many became Christian "praying Indians" at Wamesit, but after King Philip's War of 1675 to 1676 most moved north and joined the Abenaki.
